entities.name: PMID:25443702
observations: Prospective MrOS Sweden cohort study of baseline DHEA and DHEAS and approximately 5-year incident coronary heart disease in elderly men.
Included 2,416 men aged 69–81 years; 302 experienced a coronary heart disease event during follow-up.

entities.name: DHEA
observations: Higher baseline DHEA was inversely associated with incident CHD: age-adjusted HR 0.82 per SD increase (95% CI 0.73–0.93).
The association remained significant after adjustment for traditional cardiovascular risk factors, testosterone, estradiol, C-reactive protein, and renal function.

entities.name: DHEAS
observations: Higher baseline DHEAS was inversely associated with incident CHD: age-adjusted HR 0.86 per SD increase (95% CI 0.77–0.97).

entities.name: Coronary heart disease
observations: Incident CHD was assessed over approximately 5 years using Swedish national register outcomes in elderly men.

entities.name: MrOS Sweden
observations: Swedish population-based Osteoporotic Fractures in Men cohort; participants were 69–81-year-old men.
